title: Shipwreck Chowder
ingredients: 1 red pepper, deseeded and very finely chopped
large handful of parsley leaves, chopped, plus extra to serve
300g (10.5oz) white fish fillets (haddock, cod or basa), chopped small
120g (4.25oz) can of sardines in tomato sauce
400g (14oz) can of butter beans, drained and rinsed
method: Spray a large flameproof casserole dish with oil and fry the onion, celery, carrots, pepper and garlic for 10 minutes over a gentle heat.

Pour in the hot stock and add the passata, spices, salt and thyme, Worcestershire sauce, tomato purée and parsley and stir everything together. Add the white fish, sardines (break these apart a bit with a fork as you add them) and butter beans.
Pop the bay leaves into the pan and leave simmering gently for 1 hour, uncovered.
When there is 10 minutes of cooking time remaining, add the prawns and lemon juice, then simmer for the final 10 minutes.
Serve in bowls with grindings of pepper and scattered with parsley. (Make sure to fish out the bay leaves.)
notes: Sardines add fantastic flavour and are excellent value. Replace the white fish with salmon fillets if preferred, or add other seafood such as calamari and mussels. Omit the cayenne pepper to remove spiciness.
